entities.name: Agostino Patrizi Piccolomini
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Agostino Patrizi Piccolomini (died 1496) was a pivotal Roman Catholic prelate and curial official whose meticulous documentation of papal ceremonies profoundly shaped the liturgical practices of the Holy See for centuries. Serving primarily as a secretary and ceremonial master under multiple popes, including Pius II and Sixtus IV, Patrizi became instrumental in standardizing the intricate rituals of the Roman Pontiff, an endeavor critical to projecting the spiritual and temporal authority of the papacy across late Medieval and early Renaissance Europe. His work codified the visual and performative language of papal power, influencing diplomatic interactions and the broader perception of the Church.

Patrizi's most significant contribution was his collaboration with the papal Master of Ceremonies, Johann Burchard, on the *Caeremoniale Romanum*. This comprehensive text, compiled around 1488, systematically detailed the rites for papal elections, coronations, consistories, and other major liturgical functions. Drawing upon earlier traditions, including the *Ordo Romanus XI*, Patrizi's redaction provided an unprecedented level of clarity and prescription for these ceremonies, ensuring their uniform execution. Beyond his scholarly work, Patrizi held significant ecclesiastical offices, serving concurrently as Bishop of Pienza and Bishop of Montalcino from 1484 until his death in 1496, underscoring his dual role as an administrator and a scholar of sacred rites.
